results.notes: The demo fixture has no markdown (its 2 assistant messages are plain text). Three assistant messages were delivered through the fake live stream, so they went through the real store and render path. They are not demo data.

results.item: Does the demo emit live events?
results.evidence: No. The demo is the embedded fixture (source.go:14-34) with no ticker or append loop. Live arrivals were therefore simulated with a fake EventSource (addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument). The snapshot came from the real server (epoch fixture-2f1c, cursor fixture-2f1c:18, 18 items).
results.notes: Simulated events used the server's item envelope {schema_version, cursor, kind:"item", item}. The SSE id: field was not reproduced. The app does not use it.

results.item: Connection badge sequence after the server is killed
results.evidence: 9 snapshot attempts after the kill; badge text cycled through ["reconnecting…","connecting…"] (19 changes); notices while down: "!projection errorFailed to fetch"
results.notes: A refused connection shows reconnecting…/connecting… only. "offline" and "stream error" appeared only in the offline runs (C.4, C.5). No "stream error" text was seen.

results.item: Retry spacing: about 500 ms, jittered, increasing, capped at 10 s
results.notes: The first retry after a drop uses attempt 0: 250–500 ms (50–100% of 500 ms). The cap is reached at the 5th step. Failures seen: ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED, ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE, ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING (the stream was cut by the kill).

results.item: Recovery: fresh snapshot before the stream; connected only after the stream opens
results.evidence: snapshot response -> events request -> events response -> badge connected; events request /api/v1/events?cursor=fixture-2f1c%3A18; badge "connected" was recorded 4 ms before the driver received the events responseReceived over CDP; recovery 2076 ms after restart
results.notes: At millisecond resolution the CDP timestamps cannot prove the order on their own: the badge and the response differ by 4 ms, which is within CDP delivery latency. The order also follows from the code: "open" is set only from the EventSource open handler (api.mjs:30, stream.mjs:189-194). The badge stayed at "connecting…" for the whole snapshot and stream handshake.

results.item: Offline: badge text, no retries while offline, immediate reconnect on online
results.evidence: navigator.onLine=false; native offline events seen=1; synthetic events dispatched=false; badge "offline";/api requests during 18012 ms offline: 0; first snapshot after online: 6 ms; connected after 309 ms

results.item: Offline during the retry loop: no retries while offline; online retries at once
results.evidence: 4 attempts before offline; badge "offline"; /api requests during 22322 ms offline: 0; first attempt after online: 6 ms (server still down, badge "reconnecting…"); recovered after restart: true

results.item: Slow handshake text, and the attempt is not cancelled
results.evidence: 16 requests through a 4 s-per-request proxy (Host rewritten for 16); badge "connecting… @4044ms" -> "connecting… · slow handshake: still connecting @19185ms" -> "connected @24177ms"
results.notes: The first "connecting…" at ~4 s is the HTML placeholder (index.html:45), not a connection attempt. Module loading through the proxy took longer than the warning. The warning appeared 3 s after connect(), and the attempt completed. An earlier attempt inside phase C got 403 from the gateway because the proxy forwarded Host 127.0.0.1:8802; the gateway pins its bound Host (handler.go:133-135). That run is invalid and was superseded; this result is from phase-c6 with the Host rewritten. This was a harness error, not an app defect.

observations.summary: Elements dropped by a replacement snapshot are added to state.evicted and shown as "evicted from the bounded client window". §7.3 item 1 says these are source-window losses. In the B gap run the notices read "22 older element(s) were evicted from the bounded client window" next to "history evicted, the source window". The two disagree on the origin.
A gateway that cannot be reached shows as "projection error: Failed to fetch" in #notices. The label names a projection error for a transport failure.
Heading levels are demoted (# becomes h3, ## becomes h4). The code comment says so, but §4.6 does not document it.
Ledger rows are buttons with no roving tabindex, so each row is its own Tab stop. Not Tab-tested beyond this observation; may be intended.
The "N new records · Jump to latest" pill sits over the bottom of the transcript and covers part of the last code block.

notVerified: Screen-reader output (no assistive technology was run). A11y checks were DOM-, keyboard- and focus-based only.
Mobile and narrow layouts (only 1440 and 1024 were requested).
Live assistant streaming from the server: the contract has no in-place item update, so streaming was exercised through the renderer API and the fake stream.
A real live event source. The demo is static, so B used a fake EventSource fed by the real snapshot.
The slow handshake came from a 4 s-per-request local proxy, not a real network path.
Go verification beyond "go build": go vet, gofmt -l, and go test -race -count=1 were not run for this QA brief. Only the build was run.
Trajectory-view keyboard grid and the governance drawer were not in the brief and were not exercised beyond what D.3 touches.
TASK_STATE.md was not updated (the brief says do not edit any source or docs).
